programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough looks for crucial clues that help to explain how and why we have come to dominate life on earth. He traces back the African origins of humans to nearly three million years ago, and along the way he goes into caves in southern France where Stone Age people created imaginative paintings of ice-age animals. He also travels to Papua New Guinea to find some hunter-gatherers who have never before set eyes on white people.

programme.title: Shark
programme.desc: A look at how an international team of scientists is trying to change people's perceptions of sharks. Their research is revealing that sharks can be sociable and intelligent, and they could even help solve some of the toughest medical challenges of the 21st century. However, the breakthroughs come at a time when many sharks face extinction. Science may now be the only way to save them.

programme.title: Crossing England in a Punt: River of Dreams
programme.desc: From the Staffordshire hills to the Humber estuary, spirited explorer Tom Fort embarks on a 170-mile journey down Britain's third-longest river, the Trent. Beginning on foot, he soon transfers to his own custom-built punt, the Trent Otter, and rows many miles downstream. Along the way he encounters the power stations that generate much of the nation's electricity, veterans of the catastrophic floods of 1947, the 19th-century brewers of Burton and a Bronze Age boatman who once made a life along the river.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: Hidden away in the most easterly part of the British Isles are the Fens of East Anglia, a landscape of big skies and distant horizons, wild wetlands and fertile farmland. Water has always been the driving force here - its ebb and flow has shaped the Fens for thousands of years. The ancient wetlands covered hundreds of square miles and overflowed with wildlife. Today, well over 90% has gone, drained over the centuries and converted into farmland. Yet despite these changes, it is still possible to glimpse the richness of those wetlands. Every winter, thousands of migrating whooper swans return to the flooded pastures of the Ouse washes from their Arctic breeding grounds. Here, they join thousands of other waterfowl in one of Britain’s greatest wildlife gatherings. On the Welney Wetlands, spring sees ‘mad’ march hares boxing over mates. It was once thought these bouts were male hares boxing for dominance, but it is often the females throwing the punches to fend off the attentions of over-eager suitors.

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: Two-part series in which Richard E Grant follows in the footsteps of artists who have lived, loved and painted on France's glorious Cote d'Azur. Revealing the intertwined relationship between modern art and the development of the French Riviera as an international tourist haven, Grant explores how impressionist painters Cezanne, Monet and Renoir first discovered the region in the 19th century, when the newly built railway arrived there. Captivated by the light and colour of this undiscovered landscape, the painters immortalised its shores on canvas, and in doing so advertised the savage beauty of the region. For neo-impressionists Paul Signac and Henri-Edmond Cross, the region provided a vision of utopia, while for Henri Matisse, the vivid colours of the area inspired him to adopt a new palette, and in doing so set modern art en route to abstraction. With visits to L'Estaque, St Tropez and Nice, Grant maps the progress of the region from cultural backwater to bohemian hotspot.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Described by critics in 2016 as 'a powerhouse', 'jaw-dropping', 'hysterical' and 'the most shocking play on the London stage', David Ireland's Cyprus Avenue won huge international praise when it first opened and gave actor Stephen Rea the role of a lifetime in Eric, an Ulster Protestant who believes his recently born granddaughter is Gerry Adams. Here, writer David Ireland shares the story of how the play was born - from the first bizarre germ of idea that got him started, through to the casting and the challenges that came with his decision to make the leader of Sinn Fein so central to his narrative. David's recollections also include details of his approach to writing, his feelings on the filming of theatrical productions generally and his thoughts on the importance of catharsis and comedy when it comes to modern plays.

programme.title: Cyprus Avenue
programme.desc: David Ireland’s Cyprus Avenue is a multi-award-winning play and production starring Stephen Rea and directed by Vicky Featherstone. Originally co-produced at the Royal Court Theatre and Abbey Theatre, the critically acclaimed production went on tour to Belfast and New York. This adaptation mixes live capture of the performance from the stage of the Royal Court with location shooting in Belfast. Eric Miller is a Belfast loyalist. He experiences a psychotic episode and mistakes his five-week-old granddaughter for Gerry Adams. Generations of sectarian trauma convince him that his cultural heritage is under siege. He must act. A hard-hitting but in parts hilarious black comedy, Cyprus Avenue tells the story of a man struggling with the past and terrified of the future. It was awarded Best New Play at the Irish Times Theatre Awards and the James Tait Black Prize for Drama in 2017. Stephen Rea won Best Actor for his portrayal of Eric at the Irish Times Theatre Awards 2017. This recording, commissioned by The Space, creates a completely original adaptation.

programme.title: Discovering the Music of Antiquity
programme.desc: When a music score is uncovered deep within the storerooms of the Louvre, musical historians scramble to realise the potential of this piece of papyrus. The text's grammatical features give us a clue to the composer's identity: Carcinus, an author cited by Aristotle in his Rhetoric. His name is engraved on a wall in the Parthenon, and the story of his life offers an insight into the history of Greek musicians, who were revered like gods and welcomed across the Mediterranean to take part in competitions modelled on the Olympic Games. The discovery of the papyrus, more specifically an ancient version of the tragedy entitled Medea, throws open a new mission by researchers to hear the music sung through modern arrangement. But to listen to the Medea as it was heard by the Greeks 2,400 years ago, it still has to be played on period instruments. From the Greek cities of Anatolia to the Ptolemies’ Egypt, from the mythical site of Delphi to the discoveries made in Pompeii, relive this voyage along the Mediterranean coast, where archaeological excavations have unearthed instrument remains.

programme.title: Sound Waves: The Symphony of Physics
programme.desc: Dr Helen Czerski examines the extraordinary messages sound waves carry and how they help in understanding the world around us.

programme.title: Earth's Seasonal Secrets
programme.desc: Every year, spectacular seasons transform our planet. As they sweep across the world, they drive all life on Earth, bringing huge opportunities and great challenges to everything. This programme, narrated by Andrew Scott, celebrates the glorious nature of summer on Earth and the extraordinary ways animals and plants rise to the challenges it brings. With the sun shining and the flowers blooming, this is the season of splendid abundance, and the long hours of daylight make life burst out in a riot of activity. But you have to find clever ways to get your share of the good times while they last, and as temperatures soar, everything has to deal with sweltering heat. For a whole range of animals, from sneaky ring-tailed lemurs to battling ibex, and from overheated penguins to astonishing colour-changing lizards, summer is a time when the living is not always easy.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Masterpieces
programme.desc: Bendor Grosvenor and Emma Dabiri travel to the grand Georgian mansion of Tatton Park in Cheshire, where Bendor has spotted a mysterious portrait of a 16th-century physician in its collection. Initially he wonders if the work might be by mannerist painter Parmigianino, but once the restoration is underway, and after examining other works by the Renaissance master, he is forced to abandon this idea and start again. Emma explores the story of the man who bought the portrait, Wilbraham, the first Earl Egerton of Tatton, whose social climbing saw him turn the mansion into a marvel of luxury and won him an aristocratic title. Meanwhile Bendor, who is still confused by who the artist might be, is inspired by a chance remark from restorer Simon Gillespie. This new lead prompts a trip to Rome and Florence, which finally confirms an attribution for the painting and ultimately reveals the subject to be a well-known Renaissance anatomist. This prompts Emma to investigate the symbiotic relationship between art and anatomy.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Cardiff University. The specialist subjects are World War II in Europe, the life and works of JRR Tolkien, the history of Singapore 1819-1969 and the life of Henry VI.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Patrick Campbell and Frank Muir are joined by guests Prunella Scales, Paul Eddington, Gayle Hunnicutt and Russell Davies.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Japanese contemporary artist Yayoi Kusama’s work pushed boundaries that often alienated her from her peers and those in power in the art world. Kusama was an underdog with everything stacked against her: the trauma of growing up in Japan during World War II, life in a dysfunctional family that discouraged her creative ambitions, sexism and racism in the art establishment, and mental illness. Kusama overcame countless odds to bring her radical vision to the world stage and created a legacy of artwork that spans the disciplines of painting, sculpture, performance art, film and literature. Her Infinity Mirror Room installations, the first of which was created in 1965, continue to attract visitors in record numbers.

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: 'Sculpture has changed more in the last 100 years,' says Alastair Sooke, 'than in the previous 30,000.' The third and last episode of the series tells the dramatic story of a century of innovation, scandal, shock and creativity. It begins with the moment at the turn of the 20th century, when young sculptors ceased visiting the Elgin Marbles at the British Museum and looked instead at the 'primitive' works of Africa and the Pacific islands. The result was an artistic revolution spearheaded by Eric Gill and Jacob Epstein that would climax in the anti-sculptural gestures of Gilbert & George and Damien Hirst. Yet for all the provocation and occasional excesses of conceptualism, sculpture has never enjoyed such popularity. From the memorials of World War I to the landmarks of Antony Gormley and Rachel Whiteread, sculpture remains the art form that speaks most directly and powerfully to the nation. The programme climaxes with a series of encounters between Alastair and leading sculptors Damien Hirst, Rachel Whiteread, Antony Gormley and Anthony Caro.

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: Archaeologist and historian Richard Miles explores the roots of one of the most profound innovations in the human story - civilisation - in the first episode of an epic series that runs from the creation of the first cities in Mesopotamia some 6,000 years ago, to the decline and fall of the Roman Empire. Starting in Uruk, the 'mother of all cities', in southern Iraq, Richard travels to Syria, Egypt, Anatolia and Greece, tracing the birth and development of technology and culture.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: This is the story of the men who built our canals - the navigators or navvies. They represented an army of hard physical men who were capable of enduring tough labour for long hours. Many roved the countryside looking for work and a better deal. They gained a reputation as troublesome outsiders, fond of drinking and living a life of ungodly debauchery. But who were they? Unreliable heathens and outcasts or unsung heroes who used might and muscle to build canals and railways? We focus on the Manchester Ship Canal - the swansong for the navvies, hailed as the greatest engineering feat of the Victorian age. The navvies worked at a time of rising trade unionism. But could they organise and campaign for a better deal?

programme.title: The Lakes with Paul Rose
programme.desc: Paul Rose has an adrenaline overdose on his way to Coniston in the latest episode of his Lake District journey. He starts by entering a retro-cycling event on a penny farthing, before joining the mountain bikers of Grizedale Forest. Paul also relives the final moments of Donald Campbell in his attempt to break the world water-speed record on Coniston Water. He ends his trek with a spot of rock climbing at Dow Crag, before the ascent of one of the area's best-known hills, the Old Man of Coniston.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Has the AI industry finally recognised the dangers of the technology it is building? A researcher leaves one of the world's leading AI companies with a warning that the race to build ever more powerful systems could end in human extinction. Days later, the chief executive of the same company calls for the industry to slow down. This episode, AI Decoded examines the growing debate over AI safety, regulation and control. From fears that advanced systems could outpace human understanding to concerns over cyberattacks, biological threats and the challenge of containing increasingly powerful models, we ask whether the world's AI companies are moving too fast, and whether anyone can agree on how to slow down. The discussion also explores AI 'kill switches', international oversight, the role of governments, and whether rivalry between the United States and China makes meaningful cooperation impossible.

programme.title: Streets of Gold: Mumbai
programme.desc: It's the day before Holi, the Hindu festival that marks the beginning of Mumbai's scorching summer, a centuries-old celebration where the whole of India showers its streets and people in a rainbow of coloured dye. Young entrepreneur Sudipan Das is hoping plans to hold a ticketed festival for thousands of Mumbai's young revellers will be a success for what is traditionally a free event. Fashion Week is also underway in Mumbai's young and fashionable Bandra district, where we meet fashion models and flatmates, Shimona Nath and Chandani Purohit, both in their early twenties and both walking the runway. Shimona is already the face of India's most established make-up brand, Lakmé, and Chandani is working hard to realise her ambitions of making it as a model and in turn provide a better life for her family. Finally, we meet Yash Bhanage on opening day at Veronica's café in Bandra, in a city where a chapati and a cup of chai cost very little, the younger generation of Bandra think nothing of splashing out huge sums on a flat white and an artisan bagel.

However, her world is soon turned upside down by the arrival of wild dog Storm and her chaotic pack. Storm seems unchallengeable – even dominating hyena Tandala and the rest of her clan. But just when the dogs are beginning to settle into the kingdom and welcome a litter of puppies, an even more powerful force appears on the horizon – lions. These new arrivals are a threat to everyone here – something that is brought into sharp focus when Olimba's young son goes missing...

programme.title: Princess Diana: My Sister’s Story
programme.desc: In this UK exclusive, Laura Kuenssberg interviews Earl Spencer after explosive new revelations in his latest book about his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales, her marriage to the now King, her tragic death and the lasting impact on her children, Princes William and Harry.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: With the Bayeux Tapestry being displayed in Britain for the first time in almost a thousand years, Joe Crowley and Tom Heap are in East Sussex to discover what traces of this extraordinary story can still be found in the landscape today. Joe explores how the boats that carried the Norman army are still being built in East Sussex using traditional methods and investigates the region's flourishing vineyards, a feature of the landscape at the time of the conquest. Tom meets a farmer rearing descendants of the native long-horned red cattle depicted in the tapestry and walks the battlefield from both Norman and Saxon perspectives, examining how the terrain shaped the course of the conflict.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow visits Valentines Mansion in Ilford, east London. Treasures include an aquamarine art deco brooch, a Tongan war club and a rare and valuable Faberge clock.

programme.title: The Split Up
programme.desc: Aria Kishan, a leading divorce lawyer for Manchester’s elite, is poised to take the reins from her father, Dhruv, at Kishan Law, the family firm he founded after he moved to the UK from India years ago. She has big aspirations for the company, including moving away from their current premises and expanding at a new upmarket location. But Dhruv wonders if she can take on the responsibility of Kishan Law alone. Aria’s wedding preparations to steady long-term partner Neal have been paused following the tragic death of her mother, Raina, six months ago. Raina was sick, and Aria moved back in with Dhruv to help care for her and has stayed since to make sure her dad was managing. However, her family have decided Aria can’t put her life on hold any longer and decide to help by planning a surprise engagement party for her and Neal. This coincides with Luke, a secret former flame of Aria’s, arriving at the firm, and all of her well-formed plans for her future start to spiral out of control.

The neighbours say that it has been there for years, so why didn’t the survey or seller declare it? And the team comes to the aid of a single mum landed with an £80,000 repair bill after a burst pipe devastated her new home and her insurer refused to pay out.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: It’s a semi-detached extravaganza in this episode, with Dion visiting properties in Stoke and on the Wirral, while Tommy is in Gillingham, Kent.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There are antiques antics in mid-Wales when two teams go bargain hunting at a huge fair in the Powys countryside. Old school friends Catrin and Anjuli team up with expert Philip Serrell to sniff out some deals. Phil likes a big dairy bowl, but it fails to stir the emotions of his team, and they’re even less keen on a Georgian mahogany commode! Meanwhile, couple Alex and Jodie consider pouring their money into a Spanish copper lustre vase spotted by their expert Kate Bliss. They’re also taken with an unusual plate in the form of a strawberry leaf. Presenter Danny Sebastian quizzes fairgoers about his mystery object – a wind-up metal sphere with retractable prongs. Does anyone guess correctly? In Carmarthen, it’s anyone’s guess what’s tempting the bidders at Ian Taylor’s auction, but one thing’s sure – there can only be one winner!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Mark Wright and the Clean It, Fix It team help single mum Zoe support her teenagers as they grow into adulthood. With Emily’s bedroom overwhelmed by clothes and broken furniture and Harrison’s room feeling dated and cramped, the house no longer reflects who they are becoming. Extreme cleaner Maxine Dwyer leads a deep clean and teaches vital life skills, while Mark and expert carpenter Amie Williams build a walk-in wardrobe, repair storage and refresh both rooms.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Greek Job
programme.desc: Besties Amanda Holden and Alan Carr arrive at the picturesque Ionian island of Corfu. However, it’s anything but idyllic as they discover a big fat Greek renovation lies ahead.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Charming cottages and a lovely barn conversion are on the property shortlist in the Northamptonshire countryside as Denise Nurse helps Caroline from Kent return to what she calls her happy place. With the children now living overseas, this move is all about finding a home that suits the next chapter of her life. Denise also visits a young couple who are turning their dream cottage into a family home as they prepare to welcome their first baby.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee and Joe are in Alresford to help Sara and Jonny transform their overgrown, unloved plot into a Persian magic-meets-English countryside garden. The couple dream of a family-friendly space with cosy lounging spots, a chic dining area and a soft lawn where their little girl, Daphne, can play. To honour Sara’s Iranian heritage, they’d love Persian-inspired touches, from intricate tiling and archways to a striking tiled water feature, all balanced with the relaxed charm of the English countryside. Easy maintenance is a must, so the garden can be enjoyed, not laboured over. After a rollercoaster few years, leaving London for the calm of the countryside, saving for their dream home, welcoming Daphne, and facing career changes and challenges, Sara and Jonny are ready for a sanctuary that reflects their love and resilience. Can the team create their dream retreat for just £5,000?

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Buckle up with Roo Irvine and Danny Sebastian as they get a taste of Island life, crossing the Irish sea to the Isle of Man in their oh-so-charming Morris Traveller. It’s a whistlestop tour of Manx antiques emporia, where Roo takes a fancy to an entire school of glass fish and thumbs through a glossy style magazine from the 1930s. Danny tunes in to a very stylish small screen and chances his arm with a hefty item with leonine appeal. But it’s not all about the shopping. With the island’s TT racing spirit in the air, our duo detour to the Isle of Man Motor Museum, where things get just a little bit chaotic with some home-grown, pint-sized rides. Then it’s off to the very first showdown, under the watchful eye of road trip legend Anita Manning. But will it be fur or fins that wins the bidders over?

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: For years, organised gangs of abusers, mostly of Pakistani heritage, preyed on young girls in Oxford while the authorities looked the other way. Panorama examines the devastating legacy of this neglect for three survivors, revealing the extent of the abuse they suffered, the enduring impact it has had and the questions they still have. Reporter Ellie Flynn hears how the women recall being abused by hundreds of men in the city, yet to date only around 20 have been convicted. Both the police and local authority say they have learned from past mistakes, and while Oxford has so far avoided the notoriety of other towns and cities where grooming gangs operated, the programme hears how those who have so far escaped justice may still be active in Oxford.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey explores a growing looksmaxxing trend and travels to Miami to witness a shocking surgery where people have their legs broken to get six inches taller. Dr Dror Paley, a leading US surgeon, explains how limb lengthening has transformed from a cutting-edge reconstructive surgery into a popular cosmetic procedure at his clinic. Stacey meets one of his patients who decided to get the surgery after a divorce and spent over a year in rehabilitation before reaching 6ft 1in. Stacey returns to the UK to turn her attentions to a laundry powder called Borax, which sparked an international outcry after people claimed on TikTok that drinking it could cure joint pain. Tracing the digital trail leads her to a small village and farm shop in north Yorkshire where the claims bizarrely seem to have originated.

programme.title: The Split Up
programme.desc: Following the events of the engagement party, Aria is struggling to reach out to Maya. But there is plenty on her plate already, with the ripple effects of Dhruv’s shock announcement causing a rift between her and Neal, and throwing obstacles in her path for the Kishan Law move.

programme.title: The Crime I Can't Forget
programme.desc: In September 1992, Esther McCann and her 18-month-old daughter, Jessica, tragically lost their lives in a house fire in south Dublin. What seems like a tragic accident takes a more sinister turn when retired sergeant Pat Treacy and superintendent Martin Walker uncover disturbing death threats leading up to the fire, all seemingly aimed at Frank McCann, Esther's husband and a respected swimming coach. In one of the most harrowing cases of their career, Pat and Martin recall how as they dig deeper, Frank’s claims of being targeted unravel, exposing a sinister web of lies that establish him as the central focus and prime suspect in the investigation. Crime scene mapper Michael Campbell details how the truth was uncovered in the ashes of the house fire, in a case that became one of the longest running trials in Irish history. Esther McCann's niece, Esther Leonard, describes the effect these murders have had on her close-knit family and her fears for the future, if their murderer walks free.

programme.title: Wisdom of the Crowd

Briony also visits a vineyard, proving England’s wine country reaches further north than many might expect.

programme.title: Garden Rescue

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: It’s a rollercoaster ride as antiques dealers Roo Irvine and Danny Sebastian beat a path to Blackpool and beyond in their trusty steed, Felix, a 1963 Morris Traveller. Roo sets her sights on a bit of sparkle and goes glassy-eyed for a vase that reminds her of a seaside holiday sweet treat. Danny tries to carry away a hefty item that could be the start of someone’s publishing empire, and there's a box with a little touch of magic. Taking a cheeky wildlife break, our pair don their wellies and muck in with efforts to clear out invasive plants from a former quarry turned nature reserve to make space for its inhabitants. Then it’s off to auction to see if Roo’s bit of bling can enchant the saleroom or Danny’s magic box can conjure profits out of thin air.

Meanwhile, Ted suggests that he and Alexis should take a holiday to the Galapagos, but Alexis is not exactly thrilled about the destination.

programme.title: Schitt's Creek
programme.desc: Patrick takes David on a long, romantic hike, but David’s nonstop fussing starts to ruin the mood. When Johnny helps Moira move furniture into the theatre, he is suddenly caught off guard by some chest pain, sending Moira, Stevie and Roland into a panic. Ted and Alexis have their tarot cards read by Twyla, who sees something very dark in their future.

Meanwhile, David tries to make a big announcement but keeps getting overshadowed by drama surrounding the musical. Alexis is starting to feel guilty about leaving her family, and Johnny’s sentimentality isn’t helping.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s big comedy talent search heads north to Newcastle. The venue is The Boiler Shop, a stunning Grade II listed industrial building. Five comics battle it out to book their place in this year’s grand final showdown, where one will be crowned the BBC New Comedian of 2025. Hosting the evening is comic, writer and actor Amy Gledhill. Judging their performances are writer and star of Smoggie Queens Phil Dunning and 2022 NCA winner Dan Tiernan, plus head judge Fatiha El-Ghorri. Charlie Ashton, Murph, Zoe Cousin, Ciara O’Connor and Shugufta Choudhry each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final at Bradford’s Alhambra Theatre.

programme.title: Deadly 60

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the grand finale, and the remaining candidates are ready to compete for the coveted title of Britain’s best amateur sewer. The judges, Patrick Grant and Esme Young, set three challenges inspired to test their skills for one final time. First up, the sewers get gala ready with a cummerbund and bow tie. Next, it’s time for the transformation challenge, where the sewers take gala tableware and turn it into an outfit for the perfect day-after hangout, the beach club. Finally, inspired by the Met Gala in New York, the sewers must create outfits on the theme of metamorphosis as if they had an invite to the Sewing Bee gala. Three finalists, three challenges, but only one contestant will be crowned the twelfth champion of The Great British Sewing Bee.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Motoring magazine. Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May visit Spain, with Clarkson in a McLaren 12C Spider, Hammond driving a Ferrari 458 Spider and May using an Audi R8 V10 Spyder. Over the course of their travels the three presenters and their mid-range convertible supercars encounter mountain passes, ghost towns and an incredible abandoned airport, before building their own street circuit in the deserted developments of Madrid. Also in this show, Sherlock and Star Trek actor Benedict Cumberbatch is the Star in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Silent Witness
programme.desc: A paranoid schizophrenic goes on a violent frenzy in a busy high street. When a young man from the same care home kills himself, Nikki is convinced there is a connection.

programme.title: Silent Witness
programme.desc: Harry discovers Nazim's death may not have been suicide. Is Dr Sanders the culprit? Meanwhile, Leo investigates the murder of a bank manager.

programme.title: The Skinny Jab Uncovered
programme.desc: An investigation into the black market in cut-price 'skinny jabs' being sold across the UK. Reporter Pria Rai reveals what’s really in these drugs and whether they are safe to use. She meets a young student who accidentally took an overdose of the drug, makes contact with one of the most prolific online sellers, goes undercover to reveal a new market for the drug hidden in plain sight and sends samples for testing – with shocking results.

programme.title: My Insta Scammer Friend
programme.desc: In this era of social media, we are given more access to the private lives of celebrities and influencers than ever before. But how well do we really know our favourite online friends? This film explores the murky and, at its worst, toxic, relationship between one influencer and her followers. The infamous viral scandals of pioneering internet sensation Caroline Calloway have captivated audiences across the globe, with some of her followers left feeling duped and scammed. But why did Caroline's actions garner so much attention? And what do influencers owe their followers who built the very foundations of their success?

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Life is hard, so Callum and Jordan, two emotionally unassembled young lads from Northern Ireland, start the Funboys’ Fun Club: a playgroup for childish young men to engage in wholesome mucking about. But when a juice party goes awry, Callum’s ultra-religious fiancée Morgan kicks them out, and the Funboys must search for a new HQ. When they come across Marty, a catatonically depressed 60-year-old, can they bring joy back to his life and prove that fun won't necessarily lead to an eternity spent in raging hellfire?

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: The Doctor makes a final stand against an army of Cybermen to protect a tiny band of humans from destruction.

programme.title: Deadly 60

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out

programme.title: Stacey Dooley

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey tackles the subject of death by immersing herself in the world of undertaking at a century-old funeral director's.

programme.title: Origin
programme.desc: While investigating the global phenomenon of caste and its dark influence on society, Isabel Wilkerson, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, faces unfathomable personal loss and uncovers the beauty of human resilience.

programme.title: T20 Cricket
programme.desc: Highlights of the third game of the T20 series between England and Sri Lanka.

programme.title: Kidnapped
programme.desc: Powerful drama based on the true story of the Catholic Church's kidnap of a young Jewish boy. Italy, 1858. Following Pope Pius IX’s orders, soldiers burst into the Mortara family’s Bologna home to forcibly remove their six-year-old son, Edgardo. They have heard from the Jewish family’s maid that she had secretly baptised him as a sickly infant for fear that he would die a Jew and his soul would remain in limbo. Under the Church’s doctrine, the boy is no longer permitted to live with his non-Catholic family and is taken to be raised by the Church itself. The distraught Mortara family try desperately to get Edgardo back, and the scandal soon makes its way across the country and Europe at large. As they embark on an international campaign to have their son returned, they find themselves at the epicentre of a wider historical battle between the forces of Catholic authoritarianism and the political awakening taking place across Italy and throughout Europe. In Italian with English subtitles

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Datshiane Navanayagam and Adam Henson head to Westacre Estate in Norfolk to discover how a historic rural estate is adapting to survive in the modern world. At a financially critical time of year, Datshiane looks at one of the estate's most valuable yet vulnerable crops, blueberries, and meets the estate owner to find out how traditional estates are diversifying and evolving to secure their future. Joe joins the conservation team as they work to restore an important area of wet woodland, boosting biodiversity and creating habitats for wildlife. He also visits a tenant brewery and lends a hand to craft a local ale. Meanwhile, Adam meets the estate's farm manager, who is looking at ways to help run the land in a more cost-effective way through collaboration between livestock and arable farming.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek explores what lies beneath his feet when he revisits the Great Orme, the Offa’s Dyke Path and the last surviving cast iron footbridge in Merthyr Tydfil.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: The Landward team return for the autumn. Dougie is in the Cairngorms to find out how wildlife and precious habitats have been impacted by the summer’s devastating wildfire. Anne reports from the ongoing scene of the fire to see the collective effort to put it out. Shahbaz is in Tayside meeting the scientists using technology to select the crops of the future, and Cammy learns the ropes as he takes part in a clifftop rescue with the coastguard.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt delivers a tasting menu from favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Shivi Ramoutar prepares her green seasoning chicken with coconut rice, peas and a splash of hot pepper sauce. Yotam Ottolenghi dishes up fillets of halibut in a spicy tomato sauce with a tahini dressing and a side of mint and feta-baked rice. Philip Khoury whips up his two-ingredient chocolate mousse served with an abundance of toppings, including chocolate curls, candied pistachios and pistachio praline. Gemma Ogston creates a rainbow curry and spiced apple chutney, and Helen McGinn celebrates an iconic cocktail, the negroni, with a few twists on the classic recipe. Finally, either Harry Judd or his mum Emma face their food heaven. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes fishing for langoustines in the Scottish Highlands, and the Hairy Bikers explore the melting pot of flavours in Marseilles.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: With plenty of deceptively easy recipes and fantastic tips, Lorraine Pascale shows people with no kitchen confidence how to pull off an impressive meal for friends and family. Neil Forster is an impatient cook who reaches for the takeaway menu rather than making food from scratch. Lorraine shows him recipes including asparagus and cream cheese puff pastry tarts, a quick way to do roast chicken and an irresistible summer fruits pudding with a neat shortcut.

programme.title: Nigel and Adam's Farm Kitchen
programme.desc: Nigel Slater and Adam Henson join forces to sow, grow, rear and cook Britain's favourite foods, from a working farm in the Cotswolds. Revealing the top 50 fresh foods on the UK's supermarket shopping lists, Nigel and Adam show how we can get the most flavour, value and variety from them all. The duo look at how our busy lifestyles have meant Britain has lost touch with where our food comes from and the best ways to cook it. With the rise of convenience foods meaning a decline in traditional cooking, can Nigel bring the art of cooking back to Britain? Nigel cooks up our favourite ready meal, lasagne, and tries to match the price of the off-the-shelf version of this popular dish. Adam, meanwhile, sets his own challenge to grow durum wheat, used to make pasta, on the Cotswolds farm. This episode also explores the UK's favourite red meat - beef - and the journey it takes from farm to fork, before Nigel inspires us to get around the table again by cooking a supersized Sunday roast for his guests on the farm.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: A real-life drama about a family of chimps trapped in a lost world. They live in a deep and ancient forested gorge that runs though the African savannah. For 15 years, it has been cut off from the rest of the jungle, leaving the chimps imprisoned. The family face a daily life-or-death dilemma: whether to leave the safety of the gorge and venture into the predator-ridden savannah to find food, or face hunger. There's now only 20 of them left, and as Brutus the alpha male loses his grip, can the family hold it together, or is time running out for the Kyambura chimps?

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: It’s the grand finale, and for the three pairs of aspiring art dealers who have made it through, the ultimate prize of £50,000 of British art is almost within touching distance. Rejoining Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas is guest expert Matt Carey-Williams. The remaining pairs are tested on everything they’ve learnt so far as they’re thrown into the biggest event in the UK art calendar – Frieze Week. For seven days, London becomes the centre of the art universe. After competing to sell art against established art dealers and gallerists for the first time at one of the week's most popular art fairs, one pair is eliminated, and the final two pairs must pitch a six-figure sculpture to a group of industry insiders at the prestigious Frieze sculpture park.

programme.title: Cycling: World Road Championships
programme.desc: Jill Douglas presents live coverage of the UCI Road World Championships women’s time trial – being held for the second time in Montreal, Canada. Switzerland’s Marlon Reusser is looking to retain the title she won in Rwanda last year, but Great Britain’s promising youngster and multiple junior title winner Zoe Backstedt is aiming for her first senior World Championship podium. Commentary comes from Simon Brotherton, Chris Boardman and Hayley Simmonds.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and the team are in the picturesque village of Saltaire, West Yorkshire. It is a world heritage site, so with a historic pedigree like that, expectations are running high with experts David Barby and Michael Baggott. David finds six tasty sandwich markers, but Michael digs out a real treasure - a 400-year-old Laurel gold coin circa 1603 to 1625. Paul also visits Temple Newsam, a 17th-century house being restored to its former glory by a dedicated and skilled team.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: We've taken three soap stars from the road trip archives to see who will clean up at auction. Emmerdale actress Hayley Tamaddon is up against Corrie's Will Mellor and former Queen Vic landlord and all-round geezer Danny Dyer from EastEnders. Ably assisting our soap opera icons are antiques experts and superfans Raj Bisram, Paul Laidlaw and Natasha Raskin Sharp, guiding our stars to all manner of antique items. Will gets to grips with a rather unusual truncheon, Danny has his eye on an intriguing optical instrument, and Hayley takes a punt on some carousel horses. Bring on the drama!

programme.title: Golf: PGA Championship
programme.desc: Action from the final day at Wentworth as a world class field contest the flagship event on the DP World Tour. The winner at the iconic Surrey venue adds their name to an illustrious list of previous champions, including Rory McIlroy, Luke Donald, Seve Ballesteros and Nick Faldo. Two-time winner Alex Noren defends the title he won in 2025 after a dramatic play-off victory.

programme.title: Secrets of the Bayeux Tapestry: Inside the Museum
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the treasures of the medieval world. Across 70 metres of exquisitely embroidered scenes, it tells the story of one of the most seismic events in British history – the Norman Invasion of 1066. For the last 950 years, this crucial part of Britain's national story has remained on the other side of the English Channel, in Bayeux, Normandy, but now it’s coming back to the UK. A stellar cast of historians and experts follow the painstaking efforts to bring this priceless work of art back to the UK, where experts believe it was made, for a once-in-a-millennium exhibition at the British Museum.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve ventures deep into one of the most remote and biologically rich regions on Earth, the rainforests of Papua New Guinea, in search of one of the rarest creatures on the planet - the tenkile tree kangaroo. Covering just a tiny fraction of the planet’s land surface, tropical rainforests hold more than half of the world’s plant and animal species – and few places rival New Guinea for sheer diversity. The island is home to vast wilderness areas that remain little known to science, a lost world with countless species still undiscovered.

programme.title: Slumdog Millionaire
programme.desc: An orphan from the slums of Mumbai makes it all the way to the final question of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire. The police think he must be cheating, but Jamal's whole life has led to this moment.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: When a kayaker calls a friend to say she’s in trouble out at sea, the line suddenly goes dead; the Happisburgh lifeboat crew finally find her over a mile off shore, face down and unresponsive. In St Helier, the capital of Jersey, a family have had to abandon their grounded yacht, leaving four young children in a life raft. On the north Yorkshire coast, the Withernsea crew respond to a 999 call from a young man cut off on some notoriously unstable cliffs. And in Littlehampton, West Sussex, a mayday call comes in from a dive boat that has lost engine power - leaving two of its divers drifting away.

programme.title: Crossing
programme.desc: Retired Georgian teacher Lia is on a mission to find her long-lost niece, a trans woman called Tekla, who is rumoured to have moved to Istanbul and whom Lia promised her dying sister she would bring home. Lia finds an unlikely companion in Achi, the hapless young son of one of her former pupils, who insists he has important information about Lia's niece's whereabouts and who is itching to leave home. Together, Lia and Achi set out on their journey, crossing the border into Turkey and venturing into the big city in search of missing Tekla. In Georgian, Turkish and English.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Question Time returns for a new series with an hour of debate from Salisbury, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. On the panel, from the government, the transport secretary Heidi Alexander; the shadow minister for women and equalities Joy Morrissey; Reform UK’s Danny Kruger and the former leader of the Green Party Caroline Lucas.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Ash and Gordon attempt to put their past – and the cool room incident – behind them at dinner in a 'romantic but not too romantic' restaurant. Even though David and Chelsea appear to have grand plans for their futures, the old lovers can’t help but fall back into familiar patterns. Meanwhile, Lynelle and Lee are up to no good online in their promotion of WAWAM.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp meets a man whose interest in antique lawn mowers over 50 years ago triggered a passion for the old, the rare and the extraordinary. At a garden centre in Bingley, a treasure trove of mowers, film projectors and miniature cars dangle above the plants. Hoping their buys are a cut above the rest are two teams of bargain hunters, scouring the aisles of a bustling antiques centre in West Yorkshire. In blue are engaged couple Luke and Megan shopping with their expert David Harper, and in red are brothers-in-law Sam and Kier, with Philip Serrell. A pair of blue German beer steins gets bar manager Luke all nostalgic, while a child’s wheelbarrow prompts Phil to reveal that he uses one at home to store his toilet rolls! Elsewhere, the blues select a penguin figurine as an option for Natasha’s challenge, and the reds go round in circles as they hesitate over their second purchase. At Caroline Hawley’s auction in Brough, Phil plans to keep his team in touch with his bonus buy, while David serves up a tasty treat for his duo.

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: To mark 135 years of Crufts, the remaining five cooks are challenged by Tom Shepherd, owner of Michelin-starred restaurant Upstairs, to create a two-course, canine-themed menu.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Kelly Cates presents highlights of Sunday’s four Premier League games, including new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola’s return to his former side, Bournemouth. Elsewhere, Manchester City look to continue their good start to the season at home to Sunderland, Manchester United travel to Fulham, whilst Leeds entertain Crystal Palace.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 21 people start today’s show, but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for Mexico
programme.desc: Eva travels to southern Mexico to experience the magic of Oaxaca, the home of chocolate and the birthplace of Mexico’s most ubiquitous ingredient - corn. She eats the famed quesillo cheese, prepared by celebrity chef Celia Florian. The chef’s rendition is served with another Oaxacan delicacy - crickets.

programme.title: Dogs in the Wild: Meet the Family
programme.desc: From the rugged peaks of the Himalayas to the blistering Sahara desert, wild dogs thrive in the least likely of places. They are the most widespread carnivores on the planet. The latest scientific revelations reveal fresh perspectives on characters who constantly surprise us with their diversity and their unusual behaviour. These are the world’s ultimate canids!

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: Documentary series featuring pioneering images that capture the dazzling array of mysterious and wonderful creatures populating China's most beautiful landscapes. Ancient tea-growing cultures, traditional seaweed-thatched villages, bird-filled wetlands, rare white dolphins, snake-infested islands and futuristic cities jostle along China's fertile eastern seaboard, which marks the front line in the scramble for resources and space between 700 million people and a surprising wealth of wildlife.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Norwich Cathedral in Norfolk, once home to Benedictine monks, and he also visits the circus. Experts Thomas Plant and Kate Bateman pick out some gems to take to auction, among them a religious relic from France and a Martin brothers vase.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jennie Bond, James Bye, Kadeena Cox and Aurie Styla take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive travels to the Dominican Republic’s capital city, Santo Domingo, where baseball is a way of life. He meets one of the country’s top scouts, who gives him much-needed advice on his swing. On the outskirts of town, Clive encounters a congregation practising a hidden religious faith, while in the historic old town, he meets artisans who are reviving intricate, traditional craftwork. Then, he heads to the market with one of the country’s top chefs to pick up the ingredients for a seven-meat Dominican dish.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: Bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie asks the questions in the next heat as four more contenders take on the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the novels of Jeanette Winterson, the films of Nicole Kidman, the classic BBC radio comedy series Round the Horne and the Paris Commune of 1871.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Six people return to battle it out for a place in the next round – and three of them are going home. Here’s a question where one of the teams worked out the connection after three clues: Greek city law, Italian riflemen, Irish guards…

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: Southampton and Queen’s University Belfast go head-to-head for a place in round 2. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Finding Britain’s Slave Traders with David Olusoga
programme.desc: David Olusoga meets the historians who have built the Register of British Slave Traders. For five years, they have searched through thousands of documents, piecing together a comprehensive picture of over 13,000 individuals who were investors in the slave trade. Anyone can now log on and discover who the slave traders were, where they lived, how much money they made and the links between modern British institutions and the trade in human beings. David discovers how the monarchy drove the early British slave trade. He learns how Elizabeth I and the early Stuarts gave their support to early slavery ventures; how the restored monarchy in the 1660s, seeking new ways to strengthen its finances and authorities, chartered a joint-stock monopoly company dedicated to the trade in enslaved Africans; and how James II, the company's governor, becoming king led to the emergence of a new and rival set of companies and investors who would transform the slave trade.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Two single(ish) people, brought together by fate, a car accident... and an injured dog. Warm-hearted Aussie rom-com about a flawed, funny couple getting it all utterly wrong.

programme.title: Origin
programme.desc: While investigating the global phenomenon of caste and its dark influence on society, Isabel Wilkerson, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, faces unfathomable personal loss and uncovers the beauty of human resilience.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Datshiane Navanayagam and Adam Henson head to Westacre Estate in Norfolk to discover how a historic rural estate is adapting to survive in the modern world. At a financially critical time of year, Datshiane looks at one of the estate's most valuable yet vulnerable crops, blueberries, and meets the estate owner to find out how traditional estates are diversifying and evolving to secure their future. Joe joins the conservation team as they work to restore an important area of wet woodland, boosting biodiversity and creating habitats for wildlife. He also visits a tenant brewery and lends a hand to craft a local ale. Meanwhile, Adam meets the estate's farm manager, who is looking at ways to help run the land in a more cost-effective way through collaboration between livestock and arable farming.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: A catastrophic dual carriageway collision brings two patients to Southmead Emergency Department: Tom, the driver who caused the crash, and Olli, the man whose van he hit. Tom, who is believed to have been driving under the influence of drugs and on the wrong side of the carriageway, arrives with devastating injuries to his leg. Meanwhile, a young girl is brought to Resus after falling from her horse, unable to move or feel her legs. With her parents watching anxiously, a CT scan and then an MRI reveal no obvious physical cause for her symptoms. As the uncertainty deepens, the clinical challenge must be balanced with the emotional weight of caring for a young patient and her frightened family.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Gordon and Ash are feeling the guilt after their unexpected post-tapas rendezvous. Gordon tries to dodge Chelsea’s impending move and her desire to start IVF, while Ash is agonising over David’s looming proposal. Brett, with the help of his internet girlfriend, has re-evaluated his relationship with Gordon and seeks to separate their friendship from their work at Echo Park.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Charming cottages and a lovely barn conversion are on the property shortlist in the Northamptonshire countryside as Denise Nurse helps Caroline from Kent return to what she calls her happy place. With the children now living overseas, this move is all about finding a home that suits the next chapter of her life. Denise also visits a young couple who are turning their dream cottage into a family home as they prepare to welcome their first baby.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Buckle up with Roo Irvine and Danny Sebastian as they get a taste of Island life, crossing the Irish sea to the Isle of Man in their oh-so-charming Morris Traveller. It’s a whistlestop tour of Manx antiques emporia, where Roo takes a fancy to an entire school of glass fish and thumbs through a glossy style magazine from the 1930s. Danny tunes in to a very stylish small screen and chances his arm with a hefty item with leonine appeal. But it’s not all about the shopping. With the island’s TT racing spirit in the air, our duo detour to the Isle of Man Motor Museum, where things get just a little bit chaotic with some home-grown, pint-sized rides. Then it’s off to the very first showdown, under the watchful eye of road trip legend Anita Manning. But will it be fur or fins that wins the bidders over?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the grand finale, and the remaining candidates are ready to compete for the coveted title of Britain’s best amateur sewer. The judges, Patrick Grant and Esme Young, set three challenges inspired to test their skills for one final time. First up, the sewers get gala ready with a cummerbund and bow tie. Next, it’s time for the transformation challenge, where the sewers take gala tableware and turn it into an outfit for the perfect day-after hangout, the beach club. Finally, inspired by the Met Gala in New York, the sewers must create outfits on the theme of metamorphosis as if they had an invite to the Sewing Bee gala. Three finalists, three challenges, but only one contestant will be crowned the twelfth champion of The Great British Sewing Bee.

programme.title: The Edge

programme.title: Politics Live

programme.title: The Wonder of Animals
programme.desc: Bats have colonised remote corners of the planet to become one of most widespread mammals on earth. Chris Packham explores their incredible anatomy, physiology and senses to understand what enables them to thrive in some surprising places. Tiny hairs on their wings give them a detailed airflow map during flight, heat sensors on the nose of vampire bats means they can sense the most blood-rich areas of a prey's body, and iron oxide particles in the bat brain may act as a compass allowing them to find the most direct route back to the roost.

programme.title: South Pacific
programme.desc: The South Pacific islands are the most remote in the world. Their extraordinary isolation has created some of the most curious, surprising and precarious examples of life found anywhere on earth; from giant crabs that tear open coconuts, to flesh-eating caterpillars that impale their prey on dagger-like claws. Human culture is different too. The men of Pentecost Island celebrate their annual harvest by leaping from 20-metre high scaffolds, with only forest vines to break their fall. And on the tiny island of Anuta, possibly the most remote community of people on the planet, the locals survive entirely on what they can grow and catch. The South Pacific's innumerable islands look like pieces of paradise, but the reality of life here is sometimes very different, with waves the size of buildings, brutal tropical storms, and, in the far south, even blizzards. This is the real South Pacific.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from the Grand Pier at Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, where experts Catherine Southon and Jonathan Pratt pick out some gems to value. Among them are rare medals that once belonged to an early aviator and puppets that look like the Swedish band Abba. Plus Paul delves into the history of seaside entertainment.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jennie Bond, James Bye, Kadeena Cox and Aurie Styla take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: For 11 months of the year, the city of La Vega is well off the tourist track. But each February, it bursts into life. Over the course of four weekends, it’s loud, hot and colourful as visitors from all over the world arrive to join in the famous street carnivals. Clive is in the party mood and throws himself into the fun. He stocks up on local sweet treats, meets talented mask makers and prepares outrageous costumes before joining the parade in full costume.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: In the first programme of the series, Paul visits Wester Ross and discovers the heritage of Little Loch Broom. He then travels to the off-grid community of Scoraig where he learns about violin making and wind power, before taking the plunge to explore the hidden depths of the Corrieshalloch Gorge. In Ullapool, on the shores of Loch Broom, Paul learns the Russian word for parsley and how a huge fleet of Russian fish factory ships known as Klondykers used to visit the town. He then follows a red herring that connects the lochs of the west coast to the history of the slave trade. Journey’s end is on the rocky summit of Stac Pollaidh.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Join host Iain Stirling for the most nail-biting episode yet – a celebration of skill, teamwork and sheer determination. It all began with seven hopeful pairs of newbies, their pros and a beach full of promises. Now, only one team will triumph before Mother Nature wipes the slate clean. St Andrews’ stunning West Sands becomes the sandy beach battleground as three teams of sand-sculpting hopefuls face their toughest challenge yet. Our finalists – Athena and Rachel, Shane and Lisa, and Yusuf and Johannes – have just six hours to create the most ambitious sculptures of their lives before the North Sea sweeps in one last time to claim their masterpieces. Fittingly, the theme is Ultimate Sandcastles – a test of skill, creativity and resilience. Judges Sadie and Jamie are demanding height, arches, spiral staircases and that elusive wow factor. But will our sculptors play it safe or push boundaries to deliver something truly spectacular? Expect drama, collapses, creative differences and plenty of emotion.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: In Watergate Bay, one of Cornwall’s surfing hotspots, two teenage boys are caught in one of the beach’s notorious rip currents. When three distress signals are activated off the Pembrokeshire coast, the Fishguard crew race out to their location; en route, they discover there are seven kayakers in need of rescue, with winds gusting at 50 miles an hour. On one of the hottest days of the year, the Lyme Regis crew receive reports of a man suffering from heat stroke on a remote stretch of beach. And on the Isle of Wight, a fossil hunter is trapped waist deep in mud - with the tide steadily rising.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: 26-year-old Kye is rushed into Resus suffering alcohol withdrawal seizures, but ED consultant Hazel is also concerned about an abscess on his arm that has failed to respond to treatment. Hazel questions Kye about his drug use and uncovers a possible cause for his resistance to antibiotics. She consults with the microbiology team, and in the meantime, begins a different treatment. After a motorbike crash, older couple Ken and Carol are brought into the emergency department, with Ken in extreme pain. Scans reveal six fractured ribs, putting 82-year-old Ken at high risk of serious complications. As anaesthetists work to control his pain and monitor his condition upstairs, his wife Carol, who was riding pillion and has fractured fingers herself, waits overnight on a chair in the emergency department. Elsewhere, trauma team leader Jules treats 88-year-old Lady Carole, who has fractured her leg while walking her dog in the garden. With her family at her side, the orthopaedic team must first stabilise the severe fracture with a plaster cast before she can undergo surgery.

They may cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, but they support roughly a quarter of all marine life and are irreplaceable - yet they are in serious trouble. Steve travels to some of the world’s most celebrated reef systems, from the shallows of the Java Sea to the tropical waters of the Maldives. Along the way, he meets all the weird and wonderful creatures that call the reef home, including some of the best-camouflaged creatures and some impressive apex predators - he even gets a telling-off from a clownfish!
